summary.text: Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist known for formulating the periodic law and creating a version of the periodic table of elements.
He used the law to correct accepted properties of some known elements, such as the valence and atomic weight of uranium.
He also used it to predict the properties of three elements not yet discovered: germanium, gallium and scandium.

facts.label: Society founded
facts.value: One of the founders of the Russian Chemical Society, 1868

facts.label: Corrected data
facts.value: He fixed uranium's accepted valence and atomic weight

items.prompt: A chemist notices repeating patterns among the elements, and three elements nobody has found yet seem to belong in them. What did Mendeleev do with his rule?

options.label: Proved that no further elements could exist
Forecast the traits of three undiscovered elements
Dropped the need for any atomic weights
Ranked every element by how rare it was

items.explain: He used the periodic law to predict the properties of three elements yet to be discovered: germanium, gallium and scandium.

items.prompt: Besides predicting new elements, what else did Mendeleev do with the elements people already knew?

options.label: Renamed them to match the order of discovery
Removed uranium from his table entirely
Discovered new isotopes of several of them
Fixed some accepted properties, like uranium's valence

items.explain: He corrected the then-accepted properties of some known elements, such as the valence and atomic weight of uranium.

items.prompt: Lothar Meyer published a table of elements sorted by valence in 1864. What did his paper not offer?

options.label: Predictions of elements still undiscovered
A sorting by chemical similarity
Any grouping of elements at all
A role for valence in the layout

items.explain: Meyer's paper classified 28 elements by valence but made no predictions of new elements.

items.prompt: After Mendeleev's father went blind and lost his teaching job, how did the family earn money?

options.label: His mother opened a printing house
His mother taught at a gymnasium
His mother reopened her family's old glass factory
His brother took over the school

items.explain: His mother was forced to work and restarted her family's abandoned glass factory.

items.prompt: In 1849 his mother took Mendeleev from Siberia to Moscow hoping to enrol him. What came next?

options.label: He was turned down, so they carried on to Saint Petersburg
He enrolled but left a year later to teach in Crimea
He was admitted but the family could not pay
He studied in Heidelberg first

items.explain: The university in Moscow did not accept him, so mother and son continued to Saint Petersburg.

items.prompt: Mendeleev caught tuberculosis after graduating and moved south for his health. What work did he do there?

options.label: Ran a glass factory like his mother
Researched the spectroscope
Taught science at a school
Served as a church minister

items.explain: He moved to the Crimean Peninsula and became a science master of the 1st Simferopol Gymnasium.
